speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. To help you, I will need to ask you a few questions and may request some tests. First, can you tell me exactly where this severe pain is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) due to Chlamydia or Gonorrhea. The combination of severe lower abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, and post-coital pain in a sexually active 17-year-old female is highly suggestive of PID. I recommend requesting a Urinalysis and a Pelvic Ultrasound to confirm the presence of infection and rule out tubo-ovarian abscess.
